senses.definition: (obsolete) singular of thanks (“an expression of appreciation or gratitude; grateful feelings or thoughts; favour, goodwill, graciousness”)

quotes.text: If ye do good to them which do good to you, what thank have ye? for sinners also do even the same.

quotes.text: What great thank, then, if any man, reputed wise and constant, will neither do, nor permit others under his charge to do, that which he approves not, especially in matter of sin?

senses.definition: To express appreciation or gratitude toward (someone or something).
examples: She thanked him for the lift.

quotes.text: [H]aſt thou no ſhame to deſpiſe that perſone, to whom onely and no man els, thou art bounde to thanke, euen for this veraie pointe, that thou ſetteſt ſo moche by thy peinted ſheathe?

quotes.text: I can eate no meate, I thanke you.

quotes.text: The naked Negro, panting at the line, / Baſks in the glare, or ſtems the tepid vvave, / And thanks his Gods for all the good they gave.

senses.definition: In the future tense in the form one will thank someone to do something, chiefly expressing a command or criticism: to request that (someone) do something.
examples: I’ll thank you not to smoke in my house!

quotes.text: Our readers would not thank us for going into the badgerings which had for some time annoyed the chancellor on the subject of arrears in his court.

senses.definition: To express appreciation or gratitude for (something).
To respond to (someone) out of, or as if out of, appreciation or gratitude.

quotes.text: I should summon my lord from the Queen's royal presence to do your business, should I?—I were like to be thanked with a horse-whip.
quotes.reference: 1821 January 8, [Walter Scott], chapter I, in Kenilworth; a Romance. […], volume III, Edinburgh: […] Archibald Constable and Co.; and John Ballantyne, […]; London: Hurst, Robinson, and Co., →OCLC, pages 11–12:

senses.definition: Chiefly followed by for: to credit or hold (someone or something) responsible, especially for something negative; to blame.
examples: We can thank global warming for this freak weather.
